### 2026-10-10 – I started the project on October 10, 2026. At 12 o'clock I decided to get to work on it because that's when I found the time. After watching a few YouTube tutorials, I installed KiCad on my computer.

**7h**

I started the project on October 10, 2026. At 12 o'clock I decided to get to work on it because that's when I found the time. After watching a few YouTube tutorials, I installed KiCad on my computer. I started the project thinking it would be easy to quickly sketch out what I had in mind: a converter from a 3.5 mm

jack socket to a USB Type-C one. I searched for a model and tried to make one from scratch. After some searching, I came across a more specific design with a PCM2912A chip. The model was very hard to find. I also created accounts on Component Search Engine and Ultra Library, but it was all in vain. My account on Component Search Engine kept glitching and I couldn't download anything, so I started from zero.

I looked up tutorials on YouTube and got to work. At first I entered the pins manually (see the first image, where everything was chaotic), but then I used a hotkey that let me do everything in table form (see image 2). The result was that everything was lined up one under the other, which wasn't good (see image 3). After inserting all the pins, I used the X and Y coordinates and left/right settings to change the pin positions. Once I did that, I connected everything with a rectangle, then saved my work and went into the Footprint Editor, where I assigned everything the chip needed (see image 4).

After that, I went into the Schematic Editor, imported the file with the chip, and imported the other necessary components from the KiCad library. While adding parts, I also changed component values to avoid the risk of short circuits. I looked at the datasheet, then at YouTube, then back at KiCad. Progress was very slow because it's my first time using KiCad and I have no idea what's going on in there. I made many mistakes, some very basic and silly, but thank goodness for YouTube (see image 5).

I took breaks at 2 PM and 5 PM, planning to continue working from 5 to 7:40 PM. Now it's 8 PM and I'm writing down what I did, with the project sketch almost finished (see image 6).
